newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia Bakun sees 1.5bln rgt profit in 1st yr.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Bakun sees 1.5bln rgt profit in 1st yr.

text.p: Malaysia's operator of the Bakun hydroelectric dam foresees making a net profit of 1.47 billion ($588 million) ringgit in the year ending June 30, 2004, its first full year of operations, it said in a draft prospectus.

The Bakun Hydro-Electric Corp Bhd (BHEC), in a copy of the draft prospectus obtained by Reuters on Wednesday, said it expected to make an overall profit of 38.28 billion ringgit between 2004 and 2034, the period of the concession.
Total revenue for the year to June 30, 2004 is expected to be 2.31 billion ringgit, while overall revenue between 2004-2034 is expected to be 80.24 billion ringgit.
BHEC's net cashflow for the year to June 30, 2004 was expected to be 665 million ringgit, rising to 3.26 billion ringgit for the period from 2025 to 2034, the company said.
The dam, being built in Sarawak state on Borneo island, has a development cost of $6.18 billion and is the single largest infrastructure project in the country's history.

BHEC is expected to make an initial public offering (IPO) on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange in late July or early August. The IPO is expected to be the largest offering in the history of the exchange, with the issue of 1.5 billion shares at two ringgit each to raise 3.0 billion ringgit.
The propectus is expected to be issued toward the end of May.
BHEC will build the dam and be allowed to operate it for the 30-year period, after which it will revert to the Malaysian government.
The project's main contractor is Ekran Bhd, which will have a 32 percent stake in the project.
